title: api-config-runtime-scratchpad-taylor
content:
Personal scratchpad for runtime API + config sketch.

Goal: lightweight, extensible API shape for routing decisions + model variant hints + cost/latency preferences. This is a rough brain dump - iterate and sync with Samir/Casey.

Context / requirements:
- must support: hosted, dedicated, private deployments with same request shape.
- route by policy: latency-target, cost-floor, region, model-family.
- explicit fallback chain support (prefer model A, then quantized B, then remote low-priority endpoint).
- per-customer pins (model version), per-request overrides (e.g., debug/test).
- preserve streaming and function-calling semantics.

Open questions:
- How much policy logic do we embed in API vs. control-plane config? (Lean: simple hints in API, full policy in control plane)
- Best way to represent cost/latency tradeoff numerically? (e.g., budget_usd_per_request, max_latency_ms, or score weights)
- Backward compatibility: default behavior should match current hosted API if no routing hints present.

API sketch (JSON request body example included as text):
{
  "input": "Summarize quarterly results for product X",
  "model": {
    "family": "redwood-v1",
    "preferred_variant": "redwood-v1-8b",
    "allow_fallbacks": true
  },
  "routing": {
    "latency_target_ms": 200,            // target tail latency
    "cost_priority": "medium",      // enum: low | medium | high (low cost = prefer smaller/quantized models)
    "region": "us-west-2",          // prefer region
    "fallback_chain": ["redwood-v1-8b-quant", "redwood-lite-2b", "external-s3-proxy"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "customer_id": "acct-123",
    "trace_id": "trace-789"
  },
  "stream": false
}

Notes on fields:
- model.family: used for policy routing and compatibility check.
- preferred_variant: soft preference; runtime can route elsewhere if constraints.
- allow_fallbacks: customer opt-out for strict compliance.
- fallback_chain: explicit order for model variants and external endpoints. If omitted, control plane fallback policy applies.

Config sketch (YAML control-plane snippet for a customer / profile included as text):
---
profile_id: acct-123
default_model_family: redwood-v1
pin_versions:
  - route: "/billing/*"
    model: redwood-v1-13b
    enforce: true
routing_policies:
  - name: low_latency
    min_tps: 50
    max_latency_ms: 150
    preferred_hardware: [a10g, h100]
    quantization_allowed: false
  - name: cost_saver
    cost_priority: low
    quantization_allowed: true
    fallback_preference: [redwood-lite-2b]

Thoughts on implementation:
- Runtime should expose a simple policy evaluator that takes (request hints, profile, runtime metrics) and outputs a route decision: {pool, model_variant, estimated_latency_ms, estimated_cost_tokens}.
- Estimator models: small lookup tables per model_variant + sequence_length heuristics. Keep cheap and cacheable.
- Make routing deterministic for A/B testing: include randomized tie-break seeded by trace_id.

cURL example for local testing (text):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"write a haiku about caching","routing":{"latency_target_ms":120,"cost_priority":"high"}}'

Backward compatibility plan:
- If new routing fields absent, treat request as legacy and route to default model selection.
- Introduce a feature-flag header X-Routing-Mode: control-plane|request-hints to gradually roll out policy.

Security & compliance considerations:
- allow_fallbacks=false must be honored for pinned/legal routes; runtime must enforce and log attempted fallbacks.
- region preference must tie into data residency rules for Private deployments (no cross-region fallbacks by default).

TODO / next steps:
- Sync with Samir on estimators and perf table (CONFLUENCE-3456).
- Spike: implement a simple routing evaluator library in go (2 weeks).
- Add unit tests for deterministic tie-break and fallback enforcement.
- Get feedback from SRE on observability: emission of chosen_route + reason code.

Notes-to-self: keep API surface minimal. Prefer explicit control-plane configs for complex policies. Resist adding too many enums; prefer string extensibility with documented best-practices.

History: started as internal brainstorm 2025-11-03, updated after meeting with Samir & Casey 2026-02-25.
